title: 【うんちく】深海魚は水圧でつぶれない。じゃあ、なぜ 8,200 m あたりが限界？ #Shorts
description:
魚の体はほとんど水で、つぶれません。困るのは体の中の小さな部品で、TMAO という分子で守っています。でも TMAO をふやすほど体はこくなり、8,200 m で海水と同じこさになる計算。見つかったいちばん深い魚は 8,336 m でした。

アプリ「極限の世界に置いてみたら」（気圧・水圧）に関係する話です。

アプリ: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/extreme/

しし屋 まなびラボ（ほかのアプリ）: https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/

出どころ: Yancey ほか (2014) PNAS 111: 4461・Natural History Museum (2023)（伊豆・小笠原海溝のクサウオの仲間）。8,200 m は計算による予想です。

en.title: Did you know? Deep-sea fish aren't crushed by pressure. So why the limit near 8,200 m? #Shorts
en.description:
A fish is mostly water and doesn't get crushed. The trouble is the tiny parts inside, which fish protect with a molecule called TMAO. But more TMAO makes body fluids more concentrated, matching seawater at about 8,200 m by calculation. The deepest fish ever filmed: 8,336 m. Turn on English subtitles (CC).

Related to the app "In Extreme Worlds" (air and water pressure).

App (in Japanese for now): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/extreme/

Shishiya Manabi Lab (more apps): https://sishiya.github.io/manabi-lab/?lang=en

Sources: Yancey et al. (2014) PNAS 111: 4461; Natural History Museum (2023) (a snailfish in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench). The 8,200 m line is a calculated prediction.
